text:
maria: Heads up — running a staged base-image rebuild in staging and audit logs stopped shipping to Splunk right after the deploy. Getting KMS decrypt failures.

alex: Yikes. We rotated an envelope key yesterday for prod, staging was supposed to be untouched. pinging keystore folks @samir

samir: I didn't touch the staging envelope. What service account is the shipper using?

maria: image-builder@redwood-staging. Logs show 403 from KMS when attempting to decrypt. Snippet: 
```text
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z image-shipper INFO decrypting envelope
error: rpc error: code=permission_denied desc="failed to decrypt envelope: iam:PermissionDenied projects/.../locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/staging-envelope/decrypt"
```

zoe: Did anyone roll back or prune IAM roles? I ran an IAM cleanup yesterday across dev/staging — maybe too aggressive.

alex: I removed some broad roles but left cloudkms decrypter on staging. Let me check the terraform diff I applied.

maria: Audit shows entries like principal="image-builder@redwood-staging" action=decrypt then 403. Can someone run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` and paste the policy?

samir: Running now. For a short-term workaround we could rewrap the envelope with the new key and push new ciphertext, but we need decrypt perms to rewrap.

oncall-sre: If this blocks shipping, fallback plan: flip shipper to local-buffering and S3 dump, open incident bridge. I'll standby.

maria: Opening bridge: https://incident.redwood/bridges/INC-20260322-1 :thumbsup:

alex: Found it in the tf diff — I accidentally removed `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for the image-builder SA on staging. Re-applying now. 

samir: Command I'm going to run (one-liner):
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding staging-envelope --location=global --keyring=ci --member=serviceAccount:image-builder@redwood-staging --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

maria: Reapply completed but shipper still 403. KMS audit logs indicate: "request for decrypt returned KEY_VERSION_DISABLED". Alex, did the rotation script disable old key versions?

alex: Crap — my cleanup rotation disables old versions after 1 hour. Restoring key version to ENABLED now.

alex: Running: 
```bash
gcloud kms keys versions enable 2 --location=global --keyring=ci --key=staging-envelope
```

zoe: Re-enabled, testing decrypts now.

maria: Decrypt success, backlog shipping resumed. Confirming Splunk ingestion looks healthy again.

samir: Root causes we should track: (1) RBAC terraform drift removed a required binding, (2) rotation script disabled key versions too eagerly, (3) missing preflight checks in base-image rollout.

oncall-sre: Incident closed in the bridge. I'll add a runbook item: always validate KMS decrypts as part of the rollout smoke tests, and add an alert on KMS decrypt 403 spikes. :white_check_mark:

maria: I'll open a short postmortem and assign owners. Suggested owners: alex for IaC RBAC, samir for keystore guardrails, zoe for rollout preflight.

alex: Sorry team — will add a terraform guard that pins the decrypter binding and add an automated CI test to simulate decrypt after rotation.

zoe: Also propose a gated step in the base-image rebuild pipeline that runs `gcloud kms keys versions describe --format=json` to assert at least one ENABLED version before switching shipper.

maria: Great. Thanks all. Closing thread here, will link PM with the postmortem. :pray:
